'''Hagan:''' {{legend0|#a5b0ff|40–50%}} {{legend0|#7996e2|50–60%}} | title = Governor | before_election = [[Bob Taft]] | before_party = Republican Party (United States) | after_election = [[Bob Taft]] | after_party = Republican Party (United States) | turnout = 47.18% (registered voters) {{decrease}}2.63pp }} {{ElectionsOH}} The '''2002 Ohio gubernatorial election''' took place on November 5, 2002. Incumbent [[Republican Party (United States)|Republican]] [[Governor of Ohio]] [[Bob Taft]] ran for a second and final term as governor. He was opposed by [[Democratic Party (United States)|Democratic]] nominee [[Tim Hagan]], a former [[Cuyahoga County, Ohio|Cuyahoga County]] commissioner. The race between Taft and Hagan was not competitive; Taft was re-elected by a substantial margin. As of {{CURRENTYEAR}}, this was the last time that someone other than a current or former member of Congress was elected to the governorship. ==Democratic primary== ===Candidates=== *[[Tim Hagan]], He did well in most parts of the state. Hagan only managed to win six out of 88 counties. He won [[Lorain County]], [[Cuyahoga County]], [[Summit County, Ohio|Summit County]], [[Trumbull County]], [[Mahoning County]], and [[Athens County]]. Despite winning in a landslide, Taft would go on to be extremely unpopular in his second term, leaving office with a 2% approval rating, the lowest for any statewide official in modern U.S. history. In 2006, Democrat [[Ted Strickland]] would easily defeat Republican [[Ohio Secretary of State]] [[Ken Blackwell]].
